newsitem.title: USA: Italy making big effort to curb deficit - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy making big effort to curb deficit - Fazio.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Tuesday Italy was making big efforts to curb its state deficit, and that progress so far had freed domestic resources for investments abroad.
"Italy is presently engaged in a strenuous effort to reduce its budget deficit and the public debt to GDP ratio," Fazio said at a meeting of the International Monetary Fund Development Committee.

"Fiscal consolidation has greatly reduced the pressure of the government's borrowing requirements on domestic savings, thereby freeing a growing portion of Italian domestic resources for investments abroad," Fazio said.

Italy is striving to reach a 3.0 percent deficit-to-GDP ratio by the end of 1997, down from 6.7 percent in 1996, in order to meet requirements to participate in the first wave of countries entering the European single currency system.
The IMF forecasts Italy will narrowly miss the target, reducing the deficit to 3.3 percent by year-end.
The European Commission sees a 3.2 percent ratio, but adds that if all the budget-cutting measures enacted so far take full effect, the 3.0 percent goal is within reach.
